# testdata/adjudicate

Fixtures for `internal/adjudicate` (P4 tasks 8 and 9).

## `epochs.golden.json`

The recorded epoch history of the compiled epoch declarations in
`internal/adjudicate/epoch.go`: for each rule, one entry per epoch, in order,
each carrying the semantics digest that epoch was declared with.

`TestBuiltInEpochsMatchTheGoldenHistory` requires the live declaration to equal
the LAST entry for its rule, and requires a rule at epoch *N* to have exactly *N*
entries. So changing what a rule matches on cannot land without editing this file,
and editing it means appending a new epoch — which is the point. The failure
message prints the exact two edits.

This file is a visibility control, not the safety control. Staleness is enforced
by comparing a stored record's `semantics_digest` against the live registry, so an
author who changes matching inputs and forgets the epoch bump still invalidates
every bound suppression. See
`TestChangedSemanticsWithoutAnEpochBumpIsStillStale`.

## `broken/`

Adjudication stores that must yield **no records** and at least one reported
fault. `TestUnparseableStoreSuppressesNothing` walks the directory, so adding a
new way to be broken is one file and no code.

| fixture | what it proves |
| --- | --- |
| `truncated.json` | a store cut off mid-write suppresses nothing |
| `duplicate-key.json` | two spellings of one key never reach a parser that keeps the last one |
| `float-epoch.json` | a float in a signed document is refused, not rounded |
| `unknown-schema.json` | a future schema version is not half-interpreted |
| `not-json.txt` | a payload that looks like a shell script is parsed, never executed (INV-2) |
| `empty-reason.json` | a suppression nobody can re-evaluate suppresses nothing |
| `wrong-fingerprint.json` | a record whose fingerprint does not cover its own fields is refused |
| `no-expiry.json` | a cleared `expires_at` does not become "never" |
| `relabelled-scope.json` | a subject-scope record cannot be widened to rule scope |
| `no-records.json` | an empty store is reported rather than read as "nothing to say" |
| `unknown-field.json` | an unexpected key is refused rather than ignored |

## Keys

There is no key material here. The signed-store tests use the throwaway key in
`testdata/baseline`, which is committed in the clear and trusted by nothing. Real
adjudication and baseline signing keys are generated by a human, held offline, and
never appear in this repository — see `testdata/baseline/README.md`.
